episode_title: We Love Vaccines We Love Freedom

stories.title: The Original Social Contract: Vaccination as Test Case
stories.description: Vaccination represents the fundamental political problem: exchanging individual autonomy for collective security. A vaccine carries tiny personal risk to prevent massive community disease. Societies have always faced this trade-off.
stories.insight: All societies require some individual sacrifice for collective benefit. The honest question isn't whether to demand sacrifice, but when it's justified and who decides.
stories.why_share_worthy: Takes abstract philosophy (social contract) and makes it immediate and personal through a concrete example.

core_ideas.title: The Genuine Tension: Individual Freedom vs. Collective Welfare
core_ideas.description: Both concerns are legitimate. Vaccines reduce personal autonomy but increase collective health. Those who emphasize personal freedom aren't irrational; they're weighing real values differently.
core_ideas.why_matters: Helps people understand that disagreement on vaccines isn't stupidity on either side—it's different weightings of legitimate values.

core_ideas.title: Transparency and Trust Enable Cooperation
core_ideas.description: If people understand how vaccines work, see clear data on safety/efficacy, and believe institutions are honest, they're more likely to cooperate with public health measures. Opacity breeds skepticism.
core_ideas.why_matters: Suggests that public health policy must be earned through transparency, not fear or mandates.

core_ideas.title: The Free-Rider Problem in Health
core_ideas.description: Once a disease is nearly eradicated, the individual benefit of vaccination decreases (disease is rare anyway). But if enough people free-ride, herd immunity collapses and disease returns. This creates the dilemma.
core_ideas.why_matters: Explains why getting 95%+ participation is difficult near eradication, even when everyone benefits from eradication.

core_ideas.title: Knowledge as the Antidote to Fear
core_ideas.description: Better understanding of how vaccines work, what the actual risks are, and how immune systems function tends to reduce both vaccine hesitancy and baseless fears.
core_ideas.why_matters: Points toward solutions: education and clear information matter more than mandates.
